seo_title: Sixgill Sharks Preyed on Marine Life Long Before Many Modern Fish Evolved
fact_hook: This predator’s ancestors hunted seas that lacked most modern fish families.

seo_title: Sixgill Sharks Rely on Cartilage Skeletons That Flex Under Immense Pressure
fact_hook: Its skeleton bends instead of breaking under crushing force.
fact_explanation: Like all sharks, sixgills possess skeletons made of cartilage rather than bone. Cartilage is lighter and more flexible, an advantage when operating under immense hydrostatic pressure at depth.
impact_paragraph_1: Flexibility reduces structural stress during vertical migrations across thousands of feet of water column.
impact_paragraph_2: While human engineering requires thick steel hulls to survive similar depths, this predator depends on a skeleton softer than bone to endure forces that would shatter rigid structures.

seo_title: Sixgill Sharks Rise From Abyssal Depths to Surface Waters at Night
fact_hook: By day it hides miles down; by night it invades shallows.
fact_explanation: Sixgill sharks perform vertical migrations, staying in deep water during daylight and rising hundreds or even thousands of feet toward the surface at night to feed. This daily commute spans pressure gradients that would incapacitate many marine species.

seo_title: Sixgill Sharks Spend Daylight Hours in Deep Basins to Avoid Surface Disturbance

fact_hook: This single predator can patrol a vertical world taller than many skyscrapers are high.

fact_hook: This massive predator lives where daylight has never reached.
